rounds.note: Five parallel calls, one per part, render via $render so every label parses. Each call gets the full packet, explicit conventions (MET means the violation is present, permissions fall under NOT MET, no rule codes) and two few-shot references.

Outputs run long and add invented content. Add tight word limits, describe applicability as the setting rather than the violation, fold permission conditions into MET, generalise MET/NOT MET to any force, use lowercase glossary terms, and make UNCERTAIN name concrete unclear facts.

Shorten every part to the reference length. Applicability names the review setting, not the violation. MET states the permission's condition as absent. NOT MET lists concrete compliant actions. UNCERTAIN names the specific unclear facts. Ban invented excuses and copied packet examples.

One parallel call writes the whole profile, imitating the worked examples, and regex parsing splits it, with per-part calls as fallback. Applicability describes the setting, MET states the permission's condition as absent, and UNCERTAIN names specific facts.

Applicability describes the broad review setting, not the violation. MET states the absent safeguard and bans excuses that contradict the rule. NOT MET lists concrete actions. UNCERTAIN names specific facts directly. Rules without permissions get no invented exception.

Add a planning call that separates setting, violation, safeguard, excuse and unclear facts. Writers then follow these notes. Applicability describes the setting, MET states the permission's safeguard as absent, and UNCERTAIN names specific facts.
